key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within hours to days. LOCATION: UNILATERAL facial paralysis. DURATION: Develops over hours to days, may persist for weeks to months. CHARACTER: SUDDEN, SEVERE facial weakness or paralysis. AGGRAVATING: SPEAKING, eating, drinking. RELIEVING: STEROIDS, antiviral medications. TIMING: Sudden onset, develops over hours to days. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: FACIAL WEAKNESS, facial droop, difficulty speaking, eating, drinking, may have facial pain, may have taste changes. KEY POSITIVES: Unilateral facial weakness, facial droop, difficulty speaking, eating, drinking. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Bilateral facial weakness - possible Guillain-Barré syndrome, call 911
Facial weakness with other neurological deficits - possible stroke, call 911
Facial weakness with signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Facial weakness with severe hypertension - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Facial weakness with signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
